blocked.description:
Blocked is empty, or names what stands in the way: kubernetes, encryption or
llm_key.

maxIterations.description:
MaxIterations is the operator's override, omitted when the definition's own
default is in force. Omitted rather than zero because zero is not a limit
anyone set — it is the absence of one.

env.description:
Env binds the integration's declared environment variables for this
deployment, keyed by env var name. Each binding is either a literal value or a
reference to a cluster secret. HTTP_PORT/HTTP_HOST are orchestrator-managed and
cannot be bound here. Literal values are persisted as-is; secret bindings
persist only the secret name, never its value.

expose.description:
Expose opts the deployment into an external HTTP endpoint. "external"
publishes a {subdomain}.{baseDomain} Ingress with TLS; empty = internal only.

observabilityApi.description:
ObservabilityAPI grants this deployment's flows the address of the log
aggregator's query API, injected as LOGS_URL. Unlike the orchestrator's, that
address is in no pod otherwise, so this switch is the whole of the access.

Off by default: stored logs and traces span every deployment on the install,
so an integration that can read them can read its neighbours' — which is a
thing to ask for rather than to receive by default.

orchestratorApi.description:
OrchestratorAPI declares that this deployment's flows call the orchestrator's
own API — the platform agent being the first, but any integration that reads
its own installation is another.

It grants nothing today: ORCHESTRATOR_URL is already in every runtime pod,
because the k8s services module needs it for the KV store and leader election,
and taking it away would break both. What this records is the *intent*, which
is what a future access model gates on — a deployment that never declared it
has no business calling the API, and saying so now means the enforcement point
arrives with the declarations already in place rather than needing every
existing deployment reclassified.

replicas.description:
Replicas is the desired runtime replica count; <1 is normalized to 1. The
per-deployment Service load-balances across them for internal callers.

runner.description:
Runner selects the image this deployment's pods run. Empty and "standard"
are the generic octo-runtime: distroless, one static binary, no shell and
nothing writable, which is what almost every integration wants.

"agentic" is the heavier runner, which additionally carries a shell, curl,
jq, the standalone octo CLI, dolphin and a scratch workspace at /workspace.
It is for an integration built to drive the platform rather than serve it —
one whose flows run local commands, invoke other flows, or execute a test
suite. Dr. Octo is the first, and the reason it exists.

Treat it as a privileged choice rather than a bigger one. A pod with a shell
and a runtime it can point at a definition it just wrote is a general
execution environment, so the boundary it offers is the pod — not the
`cli-run` allow list inside it. Do not grant it to an integration whose
definition comes from somewhere you do not trust.

slug.description:
Slug is the user-chosen internal address label for a networked deployment
(the internal Service is octo-int-{slug}). It must be unique across
deployments; empty asks the orchestrator to allocate a free one. Ignored for
integrations with no HTTP source. Input only — the resolved slug lives in
Metadata.

snapshotId.description:
SnapshotID is the version tag (snapshot) to deploy. When the service is wired
with a snapshot store (the production path) it is required, and the deploy
ships that snapshot's frozen definition rather than the live one. Input only —
the resolved snapshot id/tag are recorded in Metadata.

subdomain.description:
Subdomain is the external host label; empty defaults to the integration
slug. Only meaningful when Expose is "external".

tracing.description:
Tracing runs this deployment's pods with the runtime's tracer on, so every
flow, block and model call they execute is published for the platform to
store. It is off by default and costs throughput, so it is a per-deployment
switch rather than an integration-wide one: you turn it on for the deployment
you are investigating.

env.description:
Env are the deployment's persisted env bindings, so a rollout dialog can seed
"edit existing". Omitted when the deployment has no bindings.

tracing.description:
Tracing reports whether this deployment's pods run with the runtime tracer on,
so the rollout dialog can seed the switch from what is actually deployed.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt and LastActivity are pointers so an unknown one is omitted rather than
reported as the zero time, which a client would render as 1 January year 1.

host.description: Host and TestURL are absent for an integration that serves no HTTP.

restarts.description:
Restarts is the total across the run's pods, which is how a crash loop shows up
in a UI that otherwise only reports the current phase.

sidecar.description:
Sidecar is the sidecar's own status document, passed through as it produced it.
Absent when the sidecar was not asked or did not answer in time.

swaggertype says what RawMessage means on the wire: bytes to Go, an arbitrary
JSON object to a client. The API description generator cannot see through the
alias on its own, and the honest answer is "whatever the sidecar sent" — this
field is a passthrough whose shape the sidecar owns, not this API.

status.description: Status is pending|running|failed, as computed from the workload and its pods.

encryptionAvailable.description:
EncryptionAvailable is not stored; it reports whether this orchestrator can
encrypt a key at all, so the UI can explain a disabled input rather than
letting the operator discover it when the save fails.

EncryptionAvailable says whether a key can be stored at all. Without an
encryption key the provider and model still save and the form still works —
it is storing a credential that is refused, rather than performed in the
clear — so the page has to be able to say so before someone types one.

configured.description:
Configured false means this installation does not have the dependency,
which is not the same as it being down.

encryptionAvailable.description:
EncryptionAvailable is not stored; it reports whether this orchestrator can
encrypt a key at all.

emptyAcquireCount.description:
EmptyAcquireCount is how often a caller had to wait for a connection, which
is the number that turns "the platform feels slow" into "the pool is too
small".

keyspaceHits.description:
Hits and Misses are cumulative since the server started. The ratio is what
anyone actually reads, but both are reported because a high ratio over a tiny
sample says nothing.

maxMemoryBytes.description:
MaxMemory 0 means no ceiling is configured, which is worth showing as such
rather than as a usage of 100% or of 0%.

redisReason.description:
RedisReason and DatabaseReason say why a half is absent, so the page can tell
"this installation has no Redis" from "Redis is down".

info.description:
The control plane behind the Octo platform: integrations and their
resources, version tags, deployments, cluster secrets, the
deployment-scoped key-value store, users and API keys, and the
site-wide settings.

The orchestrator is an in-cluster service and performs no
authentication of its own. Callers reach it over the cluster network
and the platform BFF is the authorization boundary in front of it.
Identity, where a route needs it, is passed as a parameter (an actor
id, a user id in the path) rather than proven by a credential.
info.title: Octo Orchestrator API

post.description:
How a caller holding an octo API key is identified. An expired or unknown token is
a 401 rather than a 404, so an attacker cannot tell the two apart.
post.summary: Resolve a bearer token to its owner

get.description:
Reads the db_version row the schema job seeds, and passes the stored JSON
through unmodified so a caller sees exactly what was written. Reports 503
rather than failing when no database is configured, so the difference
between "not wired" and "wired and broken" stays visible.

500.description: the row could not be read

delete.description:
Removes the workload and its addresses, and cleans up the deployment's stored
data. The integration and its version tags are untouched.

patch.description:
The one change that does not replace pods, which is why it is its own route
rather than part of rollout.

post.description:
Conversations and curated memories. Full-text today; semantic ranking replaces the
ranking, not the surface, when an embedding provider is configured.
post.summary: Search an agent's memory (runtime)

delete.description:
Everything: the working memory, the recorded turns and the conversation itself.
This is what clear-agent-memory reaches, so a partial delete would report success
over a readable copy of what somebody asked to be rid of.

post.description:
The durable record, which is never compacted — unlike working memory, which is.
Sequence numbers are assigned by the server, so two replicas of one agent
interleave rather than collide, which is why no expected version is taken.

parameters.name: userId

post.summary: Append completed turns to a conversation

get.description:
The live context an interrupted run resumes from. The body is the runtime's own
serialized transcript — opaque bytes, not JSON — and the current version comes back
in X-Object-Version.

X-Object-Version.description: the version to send back on a conditional write

404.description: no working memory for this conversation

put.description:
The body is the raw payload. Optimistic concurrency is by header: send
X-Object-Version with the version you last read, or omit it to create. A write
against a version something else has moved past is refused with 409.

get.summary: Read what an agent remembers about a person (runtime)

put.description:
Optimistic concurrency by X-Object-Version, as for working memory: omit it to
create, send the version you read to correct.
put.summary: Store or correct one curated memory (runtime)

parameters.description: Expected version; omit to delete unconditionally
parameters.name: X-Object-Version

get.description:
The deployment-scoped store the runtime calls. Values are raw bytes, not JSON, and
the current version comes back in the X-Object-Version header. Keys in a secret
namespace are encrypted at rest and decrypted here.

X-Object-Version.description: the version this value is at, to send back on a conditional write

put.description:
The body is the raw value, capped at 1 MiB. Optimistic concurrency is by header:
send X-Object-Version with the version you last read and the write is refused if
someone has written since; omit it to write unconditionally. The new version comes
back in the same header.

503.description: a secret write without encryption configured

post.description:
A rolling update in place: the id, address, scale and exposure survive. Omitting
env or tracing keeps its existing value, so a plain version bump runs the new tag
on the settings the deployment already had. This is also the only way to switch tracing on or
off, because the runtime reads it at startup and so only new pods see the change.
A tag that adds or removes the integration's HTTP source is refused — that
changes the Service topology, which a rolling update cannot express.

post.description:
A short-lived pod that runs an integration's working copy — no version tag — so
the editor can execute unsaved work. Idempotent: an existing run for the same
integration and user is returned rather than duplicated.

200.description: attached to a run that was already up

The definition and resources the sidecar writes into the workspace the runtime
watches, with a generation digest so an unchanged bundle costs nothing to
re-apply. Authenticated by the run's own token, not a user session — a 404 here
is how a sidecar learns its run is gone.
get.summary: Fetch the dev run's current bundle

post.description:
What a sidecar calls when its bundle pull 404s. Separate from the user-facing
delete because a pod holding a dev-run token is not a user.

get.description: Plain text, flushed as it arrives.

Prompts the sidecar to pull the current bundle. Best-effort: a run that cannot be

post.summary: Tell a dev run its integration changed

post.description:
The operation in-cluster callers use. The key and the from identity come from the
stored settings and the request carries neither — a body supplying one is rejected
by the decoder, which is what keeps this from being a relay for whatever key a
caller holds. Recipients are capped, and CR/LF is refused in the subject.

There is deliberately no route to EDIT one. An operator rewriting what an agent
believes about a person, with no audit trail, is a feature that should be asked for
explicitly rather than fall out of a viewer.

get.description:
A zip holding the integration's definition and every resource it owns, laid out the
way the runtime reads them from disk: the definition at the root, each resource at its
own path-like name, plus an `octo-bundle.json` manifest carrying the display name and
each resource's kind.

put.description:
Overwrites the addressed integration's definition and resource set with the archive's,
keeping its id, name, folder, version tags and deployments. Resources are reconciled by
name: shared names are updated in place, new ones added, and any the bundle no longer
carries are deleted. The bundle's own name is ignored — a replace is not a rename.

Runs a version tag as its own Kubernetes workload. The body is optional and
defaults to a single internal-only replica. A tag is required in production: the
deploy ships that tag's frozen definition, so later edits to the integration do
not disturb what is running. Declaring HTTP_PORT is what makes a deployment
networked and earns it a stable internal address.

Creates the agent as an ordinary integration, writes its skills as
resources, tags a version from the bundle this binary ships, and deploys
it internal-only. Idempotent: an existing integration is reused and an
existing tag is not recreated, so installing twice is not an error and
does not produce a second agent.

delete.description:
Clears the provider, model and key. Stored vectors are left alone: they cost nothing
where they are, and turning the same model back on should not mean re-embedding a
whole history. Search falls back to full text immediately.

get.description:
Which provider and model agent memory is vectorized with, and how far the backfill
has got. The API key is never returned — only whether one is stored and its last
four characters.

put.description:
Omitting apiKey keeps the stored one, so changing the model does not destroy the
credentials — except when the provider changes, where a key that authenticates
against the old one is cleared rather than left reporting itself as configured.

Changing the MODEL with rows already embedded is a user error the platform does not
migrate for: stored vectors carry no record of which model produced them, so a table
holding two models' vectors is not searchable either way.

get.description:

is deliberately shallow: a reachable dependency is one that answered,
not one that is healthy in any deeper sense. A dependency this
installation never configured reports `configured: false` rather than
as a failure — running without cluster access is supported.

returned — only its last four characters, so a reader can tell which key
is in place without being able to use it.

apiKey is three-state: omitted keeps the stored key, an empty string
removes it, and any other value replaces it. Storing a key requires the
orchestrator to have an encryption key configured; without one the save is
refused rather than performed in the clear.
